notes.A: The ornate block and cobbles establish the street, while the station slips off the edge.
notes.B: The higher view reveals the forecourt and lamp line, but clips the station entrance.
notes.C: Both arches and the clock read clearly, though the frame cuts into the station name.
notes.D: The signed frontage anchors the square, but deep shadow swallows the main arch.
notes.E: The pawnbroker gives the neighborhood character, while the foreground wall hides the station.
notes.F: The elevated view shows the pawnbroker corner, but blank masonry takes up the right side.
notes.G: The arch and lamps give a pedestrian’s view, but the clock and lettering are cropped.
notes.H: The clock and lettering identify the station immediately, but the steep view shrinks the forecourt.

station_front.best: D puts the station clock, lettering and arches in context with the cobbled forecourt, street lamps and neighboring blocks.
station_front.lacks: A recognizable arrival point at street level. The archways look like dark recesses, leaving the clock to do most of the work.
station_front.fix: Light the main arch from within so a warm pool spills onto the cobbles and marks the station entrance.

blind_name.name: Train station entrance
blind_name.why: A large clock hangs above pointed stone arches, with street lamps lining the entrance.
blind_name.odd: The arch interiors are too dark to make out.
